scope: Exact fixed-location joint law of all scalar radial level fields, with the independently reconstructed source topology below. This is not proof, integration, or publication acceptance.
accepted_signature:
theorem radialLevels_hasLaw (n : ℕ+) (h : ℕ)
    (x : Fin (h + 1) → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n.val)) :
    let L := Fin (h + 1)
    let P := {p : Fin (2 ^ (64 * (h + 1)) + 1) // Even p.val ∧ 4 ≤ p.val}
    let B := L × P
    let C := fun b : B ↦
      ((Fin b.2.val.val × (Σ j : Fin (h - b.1.val + 1),
        Fin ((2 ^ (74 * (h + 1))) ^ j.val))) → Fin n.val)
    let E := fun b : B ↦ EuclideanSpace ℝ (C b)
    let degree := fun p : P ↦
      (⟨p.val.val, p.property.1, p.property.2, Nat.le_of_lt_succ p.val.isLt⟩ :
        {p : ℕ // Even p ∧ 4 ≤ p ∧ p ≤ 2 ^ (64 * (h + 1))})
    let S := fun i : L ↦ ∑ j : Fin (h - i.val + 1), (2 ^ (74 * (h + 1))) ^ j.val
    let a := fun (i : L) (p : P) ↦ 1 / ((p.val.val : ℝ) ^ 4 * (S i : ℝ) ^ 2 *
      Real.sqrt ((h - i.val + 1 : ℕ) * Real.log (2 * (2 : ℝ) ^ (64 * (h + 1)) * S i)))
    let χ := fun r : ℝ ↦
      expNegInvGlue (r - 13 / 20) /
        (expNegInvGlue (r - 13 / 20) + expNegInvGlue (7 / 10 - r)) *
      (expNegInvGlue (1 - r) /
        (expNegInvGlue (1 - r) + expNegInvGlue (r - 19 / 20)))
    let tail := fun (i : L) (j : Fin (h - i.val + 1)) ↦ x ⟨i.val + j.val, by omega⟩
    let c := fun i : L ↦ ∏ j, χ (‖tail i j‖ / Real.sqrt n.val)
    let field := fun (i : L) (z : (p : P) → E (i, p)) ↦
      if ∃ j, tail i j = 0 then 0 else
        c i * ∑ p : P, angularDegreeComponent n h i (degree p)
          (fun j ↦ NormedSpace.normalize (tail i j)) (z p)
    let Ω := EuclideanSpace ℝ (Σ b : B, C b)
    let H := fun (ξ : Ω) (i : L) ↦ field i
      (fun p ↦ WithLp.toLp 2 (fun k : C (i, p) ↦ ξ ⟨(i, p), k⟩))
    HasLaw H (Measure.pi fun i : L ↦
      gaussianReal 0 (((n.val : ℝ) * (c i) ^ 2 * ∑ p : P, (a i p) ^ 2).toNNReal))
      (stdGaussian Ω)

source.title: Towards the Query Complexity of Sampling under Strong Log-Concavity and Log-Sobolev Inequalities
source.bounded_inventory: §4.1.1 Eqs. (13)–(16), footnote 2 and surrounding coefficient law; §4.2 Lemma 4.3 Eq. (27) at one x, Lemma 4.4 opening and Eq. (29) at x=y; §6.1 field notation, definition of v_i, and paragraph before Eq. (51); §6.2 uses only to distinguish exact marginal reuse from additional dependencies.

TYPING: n is a positive dimension, h is the natural depth, and x is one fixed deterministic full tuple of h+1 blocks in ℝ^n. For each i, tail i j ranges bijectively from x_i to x_h inclusive; both the cutoff and normalized angular component use that same restriction. In particular, i=h sees only x_h and h=0 gives one level.
The coefficient vector is the argument of H on the joint measured carrier, not a quantified hypothesis about the coefficients or their law.
STANDING: The paper prescribes sufficiently large n and a specific h(n) for its hard family. They are unnecessary for this isolated algebraic/probabilistic law, which holds at every positive n and natural h without broadening the hard-family claims.
derived_not_assumed: Nonzero participating blocks give unit normalized directions; vanishing blocks follow the source zero extension. No positivity of C_i, admissibility, conditioning, or angular regularity hypothesis is needed.

For fixed x the branch is deterministic; each coefficient map is linear and measurable (including the constant zero case). Gaussian laws, mutual independence, and variance nonnegativity are conclusions or proof ingredients, not premises.

definition_audit.location: H evaluates each field at the same full x through its actual tail. Overlapping spatial tails do not induce random dependence here because x is fixed and the coefficient families are disjoint.
definition_audit.carrier: For b=(i,p), C b is the set of assignments of one of n coordinates to every ordered position: one of p copies, a tail offset j, and one of K^j slots. This realizes n^(p S_i) entries, without a symmetric-tensor quotient or hidden scaling. The disjoint sum over (i,p) realizes the full Euclidean coefficient space and WithLp.toLp 2 merely retypes each coordinate projection.
definition_audit.degrees_and_amplitude: The degree subtype includes all even p from 4 through P=2^(64(h+1)) inclusive; degree preserves that value. K=2^(74(h+1)) and S_i=sum_{j=0}^{h-i} K^j. The amplitude is the inverse of p^4 S_i^2 sqrt((h-i+1) log(2 P S_i)), with sqrt(n) in the angular degree component. At fixed nonzero tails, the unit ordered tensor gives variance n a_i,p^2 before applying the cutoff.
definition_audit.cutoff_and_zero: The exact unscaled glue of footnote 2 is used with endpoints 13/20, 7/10, 19/20, and 1. The two arguments in each denominator sum to 1/20, so each denominator is positive. c i is the Eq. (16) product of one chi(norm(x_j)/sqrt(n)) per tail block. At a vanishing tail block chi(0)=0, so both the source-extended field and the displayed variance are zero. If all blocks are nonzero but the product vanishes, the same degenerate law follows. This is not the earlier-gate product, the energy truncation, or a weighted load.
definition_audit.law: The variance is n C_i(x)^2 sum_p a_i,p^2, not a standard deviation, a square of summed amplitudes, or an extra-weighted variance. It is nonnegative, so toNNReal preserves its value; gaussianReal at variance zero is the centered Dirac law. Measure.pi specifies the entire joint law, not only the marginals or pairwise independence.

source_edges.use_site: Eq. (27) turns the exact angular component and radial multiplier into the deterministic feature paired with its coefficient vector.
On the diagonal of Eq. (29), the tensor has norm one after nonzero normalization; at a zero block the exact cutoff vanishes.
Lemma 4.4 explicitly invokes Lemma 4.3, then uses independent standard Gaussian blocks and specializes its covariance formula.
Before Eq. (51), sum the fixed-location Gaussian degree contributions at a single i with all degree weights one; §6.2 identifies this marginal.
The degree sets with different first index i are disjoint, so the finite measurable sums defining H_i are mutually independent.
Combine the identified marginals with the joint independence to obtain the finite product law of the unweighted vector.

source_topology.coverage_verdict: Accepted with the refined inventory and edges in this receipt; no signature change. Explicitly separate Lemma 4.3 Eq. (27) from the field definition, diagonal and zero bookkeeping from Gaussian independence, and the within-level marginal calculation from the disjoint-family independence bridge.
source_topology.alternative_implementation: The same law can follow by grouping the full coefficient product by level before pushing it forward through the exact measurable level maps, then identifying each marginal by an existing one-level law. This is an alternative to deriving the product via the scalar degree laws; do not combine the two as mandatory source edges.
source_topology.consumer_edge: Eq. (51) still requires the weighted linear sum and Gaussian exponential moment. In §6.2, the total-mass argument uses the single-level marginal together with independence from earlier full coefficient blocks and freezes the gates before applying Fact 10; scalar-level independence alone does not suffice. The good-mass argument uses all fixed-x degree components jointly and an additional tilt, neither recoverable from just the level sums.
